body:
> **Status:** Proposal; target LayerFS v0.1.7; not a released contract.

Release: [#155](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/155).
Implementation parent: [#165](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/165).
Core review: [#172](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/172) (Stage 7) reviews C1/C2 architecture flexibility and pluggability before subsequent integration design.
Sibling pairs: [#180](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/180) (commit & history) · [#181](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/181) (boundary & trust).

## Sequencing — owner direction, 2026-09-20

Stage 7 is a review of cluster 1 (content) + cluster 2 (storage), replacing its former runtime implementation scope. This co-design pair and its siblings own the subsequent integration design; implementation and integrated qualification are scoped after those designs. #171 remains the closed core qualification, not acceptance of a future runtime.

The integration must consume reviewed public contracts so that compatible C1/C2 algorithm revisions can be developed independently and substituted without rewriting integration logic. Record any required contract change explicitly; do not make integration depend on private content/storage algorithms, SQL or pack layouts. #172's parallel-worktree substitution scenario is the review's proof obligation, not an instruction to implement this pair during that review.

## Why this is a co-design pair

FUSE and the workspace runtime cannot be designed separately:

```text
   FUSE's callback set   ──determines──►  what the ACCUMULATOR must hold
   the accumulator bound ──determines──►  where FLUSH points go
   flush points          ──determines──►  when update_filesystem runs
```

Change the callback granularity — per-call versus batched — and the accumulator
changes with it. **Neither contract can be written correctly without the other's
decision**, which is the test this pairing passes and the storage-placement
question does not.

The coupling is concrete: C1's write API is batch-shaped. `FilesystemInput` takes
sorted, unique, **complete** final bindings per changed directory, and
`update_filesystem` refuses anything else. FUSE produces per-call, concurrent,
unordered mutations. **Something must accumulate**, and what it must hold is a
function of which callbacks FUSE delivers.

## What it produces

- the FUSE operation set actually served, mapped to C1 calls
- the overlay's byte ceiling and flush policy
- where mutable state lives and what the workspace entity owns
- one mount with N workspaces, or N mounts
- what a caller is told when `commit` returns, given nothing is durable

## Already settled by discussion

| Decision | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Workspace state lives **consumer-side** | the owner must scale to N consumers × M workspaces without per-workspace memory |
| The owner stays **workspace-agnostic** | it serves "read root R" and "store these objects"; it never learns a workspace exists |
| Reads map **~1:1** | `resolve` · `stat` · `list` · `read_range` · `readlink` · `read_portable` · attributes already exist and are path-addressed |
| Writes map **1:N** | FUSE `write`/`create`/`unlink`/`rename` accumulate; only a completed batch reaches C1 |
| DB traffic happens at **four events** | create · commit (many) · merge · end — never on the write path |
| The per-branch serializer is the **merge**, not the committer | `workspace_stages` is one row per workspace; only the merge CAS serializes |

## Open

- [ ] **Overlay byte ceiling.** What bounds unflushed bytes per consumer, and what
      happens on breach — refuse, force a flush, or block the writer.
- [ ] **Flush policy.** Size-triggered, time-triggered, or caller-driven; and
      whether a flush blocks the FUSE callback that triggered it.
- [ ] **What `commit` returns.** Nothing is durable — MEMORY journal,
      `synchronous = OFF`, no `fsync`. The acknowledgement must not read as
      committed, and it must survive connection loss.
- [ ] **One mount with N workspaces, or N mounts.** One mount routes by path
      prefix and costs one kernel session; N mounts give isolation and cost N. The
      deciding question is whether one workspace may block its neighbours — the
      same question the single-writer discussion raised one level down.
- [ ] **Where the accumulator lives.** Inside the FUSE implementation, or in a
      separate runtime layer that a second projection (materialization) could share.
- [ ] **The 4,096-binding ceiling as a product statement.** A directory whose
      effective subtree exceeds it can never be renamed, and the refusal is reported
      as a cycle-check limit. That is a user-visible limitation and needs to be
      stated as one, not left as an implementation bound.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The FUSE operation set is enumerated and each op names the C1 call it becomes
      — or names why it has no C1 call.
- [ ] The accumulator's bound and flush policy are stated numerically, with the
      memory ceiling a consumer must hold per workspace.
- [ ] The commit/acknowledgement contract is stated in terms of what is durable,
      which today is nothing, and what a caller may conclude from a success.
- [ ] Mount topology is decided with the isolation trade stated, not assumed.
- [ ] The 4,096 ceiling is either raised with evidence or documented as a product
      limitation.
- [ ] Every decision that forces the owner to hold per-workspace state is named,
      because that is what breaks the workspace-agnostic property.
- [ ] No worker count, timeout or cache policy is raised simply to make a
      measurement pass.

## Boundary

- **Design first, measure second.** No claim in this pair is measurable until a
  mount exists; this pair defines its implementation and integrated acceptance work after design. #171 qualifies the core; #172 reviews its architecture.
- **No canonical change.** FUSE transport must not alter emitted bytes.
- **No durability claim.** The existing posture — MEMORY journal, `synchronous =
  OFF`, no `fsync`, no WAL — is preserved, and a `write()` acknowledgement must not
  imply otherwise.
- **Do not collapse `init_namespace`.** It is the documented multi-worker
  exception with a 2.7 s cold Init target; it is not "a commit with a bigger input".

## Non-goals

- The commit/history semantics — that is [#180](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/180).
- Transport framing, authorization and tenancy — that is [#181](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/181).
- Measured runtime performance claims — these require the subsequent implementation and integrated qualification; #171 remains evidence for its core-only scope.
title: v0.1.7 co-design pair 1: projection and runtime — FUSE against the workspace accumulator
